questions.question: Who built the rock temple of Kailasa at Ellora?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Krishna I**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The rock-cut Kailasa temple at Ellora was built by **Krishna I**, a ruler of the Rashtrakuta dynasty, during the 8th century CE.
 
• The temple is dedicated to **Lord Shiva** and is designed to represent Mount Kailasa, the sacred abode of Shiva in Hindu mythology.
 
• It was constructed using a single monolithic rock and is considered one of the largest rock-cut temples in the world.
 
• The architecture of the temple showcases remarkable engineering skills, including intricate carvings, sculptures, and a multi-storied design.
 
• Krishna I commissioned the temple to demonstrate the Rashtrakutas' power, devotion to Hinduism, and artistic excellence.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ellora Caves:** The Kailasa temple is part of the Ellora Caves, a UNESCO World Heritage Site consisting of 34 caves representing Hinduism, Buddhism, and Jainism.
 
• **Monolithic Architecture:** The temple was carved from a single rock starting from the top and working downward, a technique known as "vertical excavation."
 
• **Rashtrakuta Dynasty:** The Rashtrakutas were a prominent dynasty in Indian history, known for their patronage of art, architecture, and literature.
 
• **Inscriptions:** Inscriptions at Ellora and other historical records attribute the construction of the Kailasa temple to Krishna I, who ruled from 756 to 774 CE.
 
• **Significance:** The temple is an outstanding example of ancient Indian rock-cut architecture and is renowned for its intricate sculptures depicting Hindu deities, legends, and mythological scenes.

questions.question: ___________ dance form is also known as Ekaharya, where one dancer takes on many roles in a single performance.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bharatnatyam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Bharatnatyam** is one of the oldest classical dance forms of India, originating in Tamil Nadu.
 
• It is also referred to as **Ekaharya**, where a single dancer performs multiple roles within a single performance.
 
• The dance form is known for its fixed upper torso, bent legs, intricate footwork, and expressive hand gestures (mudras).
 
• The themes of Bharatnatyam performances are often derived from Hindu mythology, particularly stories of gods like Vishnu, Shiva, and Krishna.
 
• This dance form was traditionally performed in temples as a form of devotion and storytelling.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ekaharya:** A concept in Indian classical dance where one performer enacts multiple characters with the use of expressions, gestures, and costume changes.
 
• **Abhinaya:** A key element in Bharatnatyam, referring to the art of expression through facial movements and gestures to convey emotions and stories.
 
• **Natya Shastra:** The ancient treatise on performing arts by Bharata Muni serves as the foundation for Bharatnatyam and other classical dance forms.
 
• **Margam:** The traditional sequence of a Bharatnatyam performance, which includes Alarippu, Jatiswaram, Varnam, Padam, and Tillana.
 
• **Devadasi Tradition:** Historically, Bharatnatyam was performed by temple dancers (Devadasis) as a form of offering to deities, before it evolved into its present-day stage form.

questions.question: In which state is the Ganga Sagar Mela held every year at the estuary of the Ganga, where millions of pilgrims gather to take a holy bath?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**West Bengal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Ganga Sagar Mela is held annually on Sagar Island, located in the state of **West Bengal**.
 
• It is one of the largest religious gatherings in India, attracting millions of pilgrims from across the country.
 
• The Mela is held during Makar Sankranti, which typically falls in mid-January each year.
 
• Pilgrims gather to take a holy dip at the confluence of the Ganges River and the Bay of Bengal, which is believed to purify their souls.
 
• This event is also known for its significant cultural and spiritual importance among Hindus.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Makar Sankranti**

 
 
• Makar Sankranti is a Hindu festival celebrating the sun's transition into the zodiac sign of Capricorn (Makara).
 
• It marks the end of the winter solstice and the beginning of longer days.
 
• This festival is celebrated with various rituals, including kite flying, bonfires, and traditional sweets made of sesame and jaggery.
 
 
 
• **Sagar Island**
 
 
• Sagar Island, also known as Gangasagar, is an island in the Ganges delta, located in South 24 Parganas district of West Bengal.
 
• It is a significant pilgrimage site for Hindus, especially during the Ganga Sagar Mela.
 
• The island is accessible by a combination of road and ferry services.
 
 
 
• **Historical Significance**
 
 
• The Ganga Sagar Mela has historical roots dating back to ancient times, with references in Hindu scriptures and texts.
 
• The legend of Kapil Muni, a sage who is believed to have meditated at Sagar Island, adds to the spiritual importance of the site.
 
• A temple dedicated to Kapil Muni is a central attraction for pilgrims during the Mela.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Impact**
 
 
• Large gatherings like the Ganga Sagar Mela pose environmental challenges, including waste management and pollution control.
 
• The state government and local authorities implement various measures to ensure the sustainability and cleanliness of the event.
 
• Efforts are made to educate pilgrims on maintaining environmental hygiene and respecting the natural surroundings.

questions.question: Maha Shivratri, also known as the 'Great Night of Shiva', is celebrated in the Hindu month of _____.

__
 
• Maha Shivratri is celebrated in the Hindu month of **Phalguna**, which typically falls in February or March in the Gregorian calendar.
 
• The festival marks the night when Lord Shiva performed the divine dance, known as **Tandava**, symbolizing creation, preservation, and destruction.
 
• Devotees observe **fasting**, chant mantras, and offer prayers to Lord Shiva throughout the night.
 
• It is considered one of the most **spiritually significant festivals** for Shiva devotees, particularly in India and Nepal.
 
• Shiva temples are decorated, and rituals such as **Abhishekam** (ceremonial bathing of the Shiva Lingam) are performed using milk, honey, ghee, and water.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Phalguna Month:**

 
 
• Phalguna is the twelfth month in the Hindu lunar calendar.
 
• The month corresponds to February-March in the Gregorian calendar.
 
• It is considered auspicious for festivals such as Holi and Maha Shivratri.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Maha Shivratri:**
 
 
• It is believed that Lord Shiva married Goddess Parvati on this day.
 
• It symbolizes overcoming darkness and ignorance in life through devotion and meditation.
 
• Many followers meditate and practice yoga to deepen their spiritual connection.
 
 
 
• **Shiva Lingam Worship:**
 
 
• The Shiva Lingam represents the union of Shiva and Shakti, symbolizing cosmic energy and creation.
 
• Offerings such as milk, honey, and bilva leaves are made during Maha Shivratri.
 
 
 
• **Fasting Rituals:**
 
 
• Devotees observe a strict fast, abstaining from grains and consuming fruits and water.
 
• Staying awake throughout the night is considered auspicious, symbolizing vigilance and spiritual awakening.

questions.question: The sacred journey of Lord Jagannath with brother Balabhadra and sister Subhadra from the Jagannath Temple of Puri, popularly known as ‘Rath Yatra’, starts in the Hindu month of _____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ashadha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Rath Yatra of Lord Jagannath is an annual festival that takes place in Puri, Odisha.
 
• It begins in the Hindu month of Ashadha, which typically falls in June or July.
 
• The festival involves the procession of deities Jagannath, Balabhadra, and Subhadra in chariots from the Jagannath Temple to the Gundicha Temple.
 
• Millions of devotees participate in the Rath Yatra, making it one of the largest religious gatherings in the world.
 
• The event is celebrated with great enthusiasm, featuring elaborate rituals, prayers, and cultural programs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jagannath Temple:**

 
 
• Located in Puri, Odisha, it is one of the four sacred Char Dham pilgrimage sites in India.
 
• The temple is dedicated to Lord Jagannath, an incarnation of Lord Vishnu.
 
• It was constructed in the 12th century by King Anantavarman Chodaganga Deva.
 
 
 
• **Chariots:**
 
 
• Three colossal chariots are constructed annually for the procession, each dedicated to a deity.
 
• The chariots are made of wood and decorated with intricate designs and colorful fabrics.
 
• The pulling of the chariots by devotees is considered highly auspicious.
 
 
 
• **Gundicha Temple:**
 
 
• Located about 3 km from the Jagannath Temple, it is the destination of the Rath Yatra procession.
 
• The deities reside in the Gundicha Temple for a period of 9 days before returning to the main temple.
 
 
 
• **Significance:**
 
 
• The Rath Yatra symbolizes the annual visit of Lord Jagannath to his birthplace, Gundicha Temple.
 
• It represents the journey of the soul towards spiritual salvation.
 
• The festival promotes unity and devotion among the followers of Lord Jagannath.

questions.question: The traditional Hindu festival of Chhath, observed by people all over Bihar, Jharkhand and parts of Uttar Pradesh, takes place after the festival of _____
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Diwali**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Chhath Puja is celebrated six days after the festival of **Diwali**.
 
• The festival is primarily observed in the Indian states of **Bihar, Jharkhand, and parts of Uttar Pradesh**, as well as in Nepal.
 
• Chhath Puja is dedicated to the **Sun God (Surya) and his wife Usha** to thank them for bestowing life on earth and to request the granting of certain wishes.
 
• It involves rituals such as **holy bathing, fasting, standing in water for long periods**, and offering prasad (prayer offerings).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Significance of Chhath Puja**

 
 
• Chhath Puja is one of the oldest festivals dedicated to the Sun God, dating back to ancient Vedic times.
 
• The festival signifies the **importance of solar energy** in sustaining life on earth.
 
 
 
• **Rituals and Practices**
 
 
• The rituals are rigorous and include fasting, abstaining from drinking water, standing in water, and offering arghya to the setting and rising sun.
 
• Devotees also prepare a special prasad, including **thekua**, a type of sweet dish made from wheat flour.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Aspect**
 
 
• Chhath Puja emphasizes the importance of cleanliness and environmental preservation, with devotees often cleaning riverbanks and water bodies.
 
 
 
• **Global Observance**
 
 
• Though primarily observed in India and Nepal, Chhath Puja has gained popularity among the Indian diaspora in various countries including the United States, United Kingdom, and Mauritius.

• Supports the protection and preservation of cultural heritage worldwide.

questions.question: In Tamil Nadu, which day of Pongal is celebrated as Kaanum Pongal?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fourth**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Kaanum Pongal is celebrated on the fourth day of the Pongal festival in Tamil Nadu.
 
• This day is dedicated to social gatherings, outdoor activities, and visiting relatives and friends.
 
• People often visit beaches and temples and engage in various recreational activities on this day.
 
• Kaanum Pongal signifies the end of the Pongal festival and is a day of relaxation and enjoyment after the previous days of celebrations and rituals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pongal Festival:**

 
 
• Pongal is a four-day harvest festival celebrated in Tamil Nadu, marking the end of the winter solstice.
 
• The festival is dedicated to the Sun God and is observed with a variety of traditional rituals and customs.
 
• It typically occurs in mid-January, coinciding with the Tamil month of Thai.
 
• Each day of the festival has its own significance: Bhogi Pongal, Surya Pongal, Mattu Pongal, and Kaanum Pongal.
 
 
 
• **Bhogi Pongal:**
 
 
• The first day of the Pongal festival, dedicated to Lord Indra, the god of rain.
 
• People clean their homes and light bonfires to discard old belongings, symbolizing new beginnings.
 
 
 
• **Surya Pongal:**
 
 
• The second day, dedicated to the Sun God, Surya, where new rice is boiled in milk and offered to the deity.
 
• The dish is known as 'Pongal' and is a central part of the celebrations.
 
 
 
• **Mattu Pongal:**
 
 
• The third day, dedicated to cattle, especially bulls, which play a vital role in agriculture.
 
• Cattle are decorated, honored, and worshipped for their contribution to the farming community.

questions.question: Which of the following festivals marks the birth of Prince Siddhartha Gautama, who founded a religion?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Buddha Purnima**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Buddha Purnima**, also known as Vesak, commemorates the birth, enlightenment, and death (Mahaparinirvana) of Gautama Buddha.
 
• The festival is celebrated on the full moon day (Purnima) in the Hindu month of Vaishakha (April-May).
 
• It marks the birth anniversary of **Prince Siddhartha Gautama**, who later became Gautama Buddha, the founder of Buddhism.
 
• Buddha Purnima is observed by Buddhists across the world, especially in countries like India, Nepal, Sri Lanka, Bhutan, and Southeast Asian nations.
 
• The day is significant for Buddhists, as it symbolizes the teachings of Buddha and his path toward liberation from suffering.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Prince Siddhartha Gautama:**

 
 
• Born in Lumbini (present-day Nepal) in 563 BCE to King Suddhodana and Queen Maya Devi.
 
• Renounced royal life at the age of 29 to seek answers to life's suffering.
 
• Attained enlightenment under the Bodhi Tree in Bodh Gaya, India, becoming the Buddha ("The Enlightened One").
 
 
 
• **Core Teachings of Buddha:**
 
 
• The Four Noble Truths: Dukkha (suffering), Samudaya (cause of suffering), Nirodha (end of suffering), and Magga (path to cessation of suffering).

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct about Kati Bihu, one of the three Bihus celebrated especially in the state of Assam?

• Farmers light earthen lamps (diyas) in their fields, granaries, and at the base of tulsi plants, symbolizing hope and devotion for a good harvest.

questions.question:

questions.solution:

__
 
• **Saga Dawa** is the most sacred Buddhist festival, commemorating the birth, enlightenment, and Mahaparinirvana (passing away) of Buddha Shakyamuni.
 
• The festival is celebrated on the full moon day of the fourth month in the Tibetan lunar calendar, typically falling in May or June in the Gregorian calendar.
 
• It is also known as the "Month of Merits," during which Buddhists engage in acts of generosity, prayer, and meditation to accumulate positive karma.
 
• In the Tibetan tradition, Saga Dawa is marked with rituals such as hoisting prayer flags, visiting monasteries, and circumambulating holy sites like stupas and mountains.
 
• The festival holds significant importance in the Himalayan regions of Tibet, Bhutan, Nepal, and parts of India such as Ladakh, Sikkim, and Arunachal Pradesh.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mahaparinirvana:** Refers to the final passing away of Buddha Shakyamuni, symbolizing his liberation from the cycle of birth and death (samsara).
 
• **Enlightenment:** Buddha attained enlightenment under the Bodhi tree in Bodh Gaya, realizing the Four Noble Truths and the Eightfold Path.
 
• **Acts of Merit:** During Saga Dawa, Buddhists engage in activities like offering alms, saving animals from slaughter, and reciting scriptures to accumulate spiritual benefits.
 
• **Prayer Flags:** Colorful flags inscribed with mantras and prayers are hoisted to spread peace, compassion, and blessings into the surrounding environment.
 
• **Other Buddhist Festivals:** Apart from Saga Dawa, Vesak (Buddha Purnima) is another widely celebrated festival marking the same three events in Buddha's life, observed across South and Southeast Asia.

questions.question: For how many days is the Goa Carnival organised, where elaborate and brilliantly coloured floats, music and dancing form part of the Carnival extravaganza in Goa?

• The Carnival is marked by parades on the streets of Goa's major cities like Panaji, Margao, Vasco, and Mapusa.
 
• One of the main highlights is the **"King Momo"** parade, where a symbolic figure leads the festivities, calling for merriment and enjoyment.

• The Goa Carnival traces its roots back to the Portuguese colonial era, which lasted for over 450 years.
 
• It was introduced as a pre-Lenten festival to mark indulgence before the fasting period of Lent in Christianity.
 
 
 
• **Significance of King Momo:**
 
 
• King Momo is a traditional figure representing fun and frolic, and his proclamation signals the official start of the Carnival celebrations.
 
• King Momo is usually portrayed by a local individual chosen for his lively and spirited personality.
 
 
 
• **Tourism Impact:**

questions.question: Shyama Shastri, Tyagaraja and Muthuswami Dikshitar, the three composer-musicians of the 18th century, are considered as the trinity of _____ classical music form of India.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Carnatic**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Shyama Shastri, Tyagaraja, and Muthuswami Dikshitar are regarded as the trinity of **Carnatic music**, one of the two major classical music traditions of India.
 
• They lived in the 18th century and contributed significantly to the development of Carnatic music through their compositions, which are still widely performed today.
 
• Tyagaraja is best known for his devotional compositions, primarily in praise of Lord Rama, with over 700 kritis attributed to him.
 
• Shyama Shastri composed numerous kritis, varnams, and other forms, often dedicated to Goddess Kamakshi.
 
• Muthuswami Dikshitar was renowned for his scholarly approach, composing kritis in Sanskrit and incorporating influences from both Indian and Western music.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Carnatic Music:**

 
 
• Carnatic music is a system of classical music associated with the southern part of India, emphasizing vocal-based compositions.
 
• The compositions, known as kritis, are often devotional in nature, dedicated to Hindu deities.
 
• It is characterized by intricate raga (melodic frameworks) and tala (rhythmic cycles).
 
 
 
• **Hindustani Music:**
 
 
• The other major classical music tradition of India, primarily practiced in the northern region.
 
• Unlike Carnatic music, Hindustani music places greater emphasis on improvisation during performance.
 
 
 
• **Concept of Trinity:**
 
 
• The "Trinity" concept in Carnatic music refers to these three legendary composers whose works set the foundation for modern Carnatic music performances.
 
• They are considered equivalent to saints for their spiritual and musical contributions.
 
 
 
• **Musical Forms:**
 
 
• Common forms in Carnatic music include kritis, varnams, and padams, each serving different purposes in a concert setting.
 
• The kritis of the Trinity are celebrated for their lyrical beauty, structural perfection, and deep emotional resonance.

questions.question: Grammy award winner, Carnatic musician Thetakudi Harihara Vinayakram, fondly known as Vikku, is known for his mastery of which of the following musical instruments?

__
 
• Thetakudi Harihara Vinayakram, popularly known as Vikku, is a globally renowned **Carnatic percussionist** specializing in the Ghatam.
 
• The Ghatam is a traditional South Indian percussion instrument made of clay, often used in **Carnatic music concerts**.
 
• Vikku Vinayakram is the first South Indian musician to win the prestigious **Grammy Award** for his work in the album "Planet Drum" with Mickey Hart in 1991.
 
• He is celebrated for introducing the Ghatam to a global audience and **revolutionizing its playing techniques** by incorporating innovative rhythms and styles.

• **Ghatam**

 
 
• The Ghatam is a percussion instrument typically made of baked clay mixed with metals like copper, iron, and brass to enhance its tonal quality.
 
• The instrument has no membrane and produces sound by striking its surface with fingers, palms, and nails.
 
• It is known for its **unique resonant sound** and is often tuned to match the key of the performance.
 
• Playing the Ghatam requires advanced skills, including hand coordination and control over tonal variations.
 
 
 
• **Carnatic Music**
 
 
• Carnatic music is one of the two major traditions of Indian classical music, the other being Hindustani music.
 
• It is primarily practiced in South India and emphasizes **improvisation and intricate rhythmic patterns**.
 
• Key instruments in Carnatic music include the Veena, Mridangam, Ghatam, and Violin.
 
• Concerts usually follow a structured format, beginning with a varnam and culminating in a thillana.
 
 
 
• **Grammy Awards**
 
 
• The Grammy Awards are prestigious accolades presented by the Recording Academy to recognize excellence in the music industry.
 
• Vikku Vinayakram's Grammy win in 1991 brought global recognition to Indian classical percussion instruments.
 
• Indian artists like Pandit Ravi Shankar, Zakir Hussain, and A.R. Rahman have also been honored with Grammy Awards.
 
 
 
• **Fusion Music**

• Vikku Vinayakram has been a pioneer in blending Carnatic music with **world music**, collaborating with artists like John McLaughlin in Shakti.
 
• Such collaborations have played a vital role in introducing Indian classical music to global audiences.
